title: River mini-game: Qwen3.8-27B on a Mac Studio vs a DGX Spark, thinking off and on
prompt:
Create a single self-contained HTML file: a three.js mini-game where the player shapes a river. Load three.js and OrbitControls from a CDN via an import map; no other assets.

- Terrain: a 128x128 heightfield valley sloping from one edge to the opposite edge, rendered as a lit mesh with grass, dirt and rock colouring by height and slope.
- Water: simulate it on the same grid (shallow-water or virtual-pipe heightfield, not a pre-drawn path). A spring at the high edge adds water every step; water drains off the low edge. Render depth as a translucent surface above the terrain, lighter or foamy where it moves fast.
- Tools: left-drag raises terrain (drop rocks/land); shift-drag or right-drag lowers it (dig). A brush-size slider. Water must visibly find a new path within a few seconds of a change.
- Flow: a slider plus the +/- keys set spring rate from 0 (the river dries up) to high (it floods its banks).
- HUD: flow rate, total water volume, FPS, a Reset button.
- Camera: orbit with the middle mouse or while holding Space, so it doesn't fight the tools. Keep the sim stable at any setting; clamp so it never blows up.

Output only the HTML.

sampling.note: Identical request on both machines. max_tokens 196,000 fits inside the Spark's 196,608 serving window (the largest window run on that box after a 262,144 window hung it earlier the same day); the Mac served 262,144.

serving.mac: Mac Studio M4 Max 128 GB, MLX lane engine, --context 262144
serving.spark: one DGX Spark GB10 (spark-b610), NVIDIA pytorch:26.07-py3 container, CUDA engine, --context 196608, host-memory guard (never fired; >=78 GiB available throughout)
serving.determinism: Same seed on Metal and CUDA diverges early; each machine's output is its own generation, not a re-render of the other.

spark-think-on-s43.verdict_by_eye: Best of the eight. A winding river over lit, textured terrain; flow 0 shrinks it (HUD: "seeping away"), max floods the low end into a lake; the ridge and dig shift its shape a little. Zero console errors.

spark-think-on-s42.verdict_by_eye: Good. Clean lit scene and HUD; water collects into a valley lake and the volume readout climbs 562 → 5,195 with flow. Rerouting around the ridge/dig is not obvious in the clip.

mac-think-off-s43.verdict_by_eye: Partial. Terrain renders near-black, but channels show and the ridge visibly raises ground with water spreading around it.

mac-think-on-s42.verdict_by_eye: Partial. Coloured terrain; water pools and grows at max flow — floods like a lake rather than a river.

mac-think-on-s43.verdict_by_eye: Weak. The valley sits under a sheet of water even at flow 0.

mac-think-off-s42.verdict_by_eye: Weak. Polished HUD, but terrain renders near-black and there is one streak of water; the flow slider has no visible effect in the clip.

spark-think-off-s42.verdict_by_eye: Weak. Near-black terrain, HUD prints raw <small> tags, a faint patch of water.

spark-think-off-s43.verdict_by_eye: Broken as shipped: `water` declared twice (a Float32Array and the water mesh), so the module never runs. Two one-line fixes tried (rename the mesh; a for-loop that never incremented x); a third error then appeared (water volume goes NaN, TypeError every frame) and the repair was stopped per the three-error rule. The playable link is the untouched original.

recording.method: Headless Chromium (ANGLE/Metal) 1280x720, deterministic 24 fps clock shim, 32 s per arm, identical scripted input on every arm: 0-6 s idle; 6 s flow slider to minimum; 12 s to maximum; 18 s to middle + a 2.1 s left-drag ridge across screen centre; 25 s a shift+left diagonal dig. Flow slider found by label; every arm's slider was found. Math.random pinned to a fixed LCG on the capture side only; published files untouched.
recording.caveat: The fixed clock steps each game at 24 fps; a game that scales its simulation by real frame time will evolve at its own pace, and some rerouting may happen after the 32 s window.
